messages:
Lena (AE): AtlasAI POC finished. TL;DR: steady 300 qps, two 3-min spikes to 900 qps. p50 ~= 30ms, p95 ~= 110ms, p99 up to ~600ms during spike ramps. Customer wants: 1) short explanation for p99 ramp 2) conservative cost delta for 4x burst headroom (10 mins/day) for procurement slide 3) BYOK/KMS impact note. Can we assemble an ops+pricing one-pager by EOD? :hourglass: 

Marco (SRE): Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-poc/atlasai/1848887777/ (heatmap.png, traces.tar.gz, loadprofile.json)

Ivy (Eng): Load profile pasted below (from loadprofile.json):
```json
{"phases":[{"duration_s":1200,"qps":300},{"duration_s":180,"qps":900},{"duration_s":180,"qps":900},{"duration_s":600,"qps":300}],"avg_tokens":350,"prompt_shape":"chat_turns=3"}
```

Ivy (Eng): Quick analysis: tail aligns with spike ramp and with a correlated increase in batch size at ramp start. We saw one AZ trigger extra replica provisioning causing ~12-18s readiness in that AZ which maps to the p99 windows. Two main mitigations: prewarm small pool of warm replicas (staggered across AZs) and prefill KV prefix cache for top-200 prefixes. Also limit max_batch_size during expected ramp to keep latency for short requests bounded.

Marco (SRE): Test infra: dedicated nvidia-a100-small x4 across 3 AZs. Autoscaler annotation hit in AZ-b when spike started. Recommended quick config changes: 
- min_replicas=2 per AZ
- buffer_replicas=1 per AZ (to avoid synchronous scale to zero->many)
- prewarm_count=6 (distribute across AZs) with prewarm_window=90s
I'll add a PR to runbooks with prewarm scripts. Example prewarm we used: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @sample_small.json &
done
```

Sam (Security): BYOK/KMS note: with customer-managed keys we measured additional latency in tests ~7-16ms per request depending on KMS region and key policy. Options: envelope key caching (recommended window 20-60s) to reduce per-request KMS calls, and audit-log export for compliance. I will start the vendor questionnaire responses and include the cache tradeoffs and rotation cadence. If they require HSM attestation we'll escalate to Legal.

Lena (AE): Pricing ask: procurement wants a single conservative number for the renewal slide comparing worst-case on-demand vs 12mo reserved commit for 4x burst headroom (10 min/day). Can we give those numbers with assumptions?

Ivy (Eng): Ballpark cost delta (assumptions: current footprint baseline on A100 family, 4x peak for 10min/day): 
- Worst-case on-demand: +35% monthly (heavy transient scale spikes + more prewarm if using on-demand)
- Committed 12mo reserved: +9% monthly (buffer replicas + small idle prewarm)
I'll produce a short table with A100 vs A10G estimates and conservative rounding for procurement.

Marco (SRE): Addendum: if they accept routing 20% of burst to a lighter quantized model variant we can shave ~8-12% off the on-demand worst-case. Note quality tradeoffs; include A/B check suggestion.

Sam (Security): For the one-pager I'll add a short measured KMS latency range (7-16ms), recommended envelope caching pattern, and audit export options. Also include language about rotating cached envelopes and the short security review required for caching windows.

Ivy (Eng): I'll assemble the one-pager: sections = Summary, Observations (p99 cause), Mitigations (prewarm, buffer replicas, batch cap, KV prefill), Cost delta (on-demand vs reserved), BYOK note, Next steps + action owners. Target draft in ~3 hours.

Lena (AE): Great. Action items: Ivy to send draft, Marco to PR runbook prewarm scripts, Sam to start vendor QA, Ivy + Marco to attach cost spreadsheet. Need final to send to customer by 5pm PT today.

Marco (SRE): I'll open a short internal canary checklist for rollout: small canary traffic (2%) for 30 minutes, monitor p99 and KMS metrics, rollback route if p99 > 2x baseline.

Lena (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll prep the procurement slide with the conservative +35% and reserved +9% numbers pending Ivy's spreadsheet.

Ivy (Eng): Spreadsheet and draft one-pager will be uploaded to the artifact path shortly.
